title: fix(e2e/live): start-backend.sh records the server's pid, not a subshell's (objectui#12676)
body:
Fixes #12676

Clause-②: no

`e2e/live/ci/start-backend.sh` now writes the PID of the `objectstack dev` process itself to `backend.pid`. So `e2e/live/ci/stop-backend.sh` stops the server it started, and the port goes quiet. Before, the script backgrounded the whole `cd … && nohup …` list, and `$!` was the PID of a forked bash subshell that waited on the server. The stop script killed that subshell, and the server, reparented to PID 1, kept the port.

## The fix

One hunk in `start()`. The `cd "$APP_DIR"` now runs first inside the parenthesised subshell, and only the `nohup …` command is backgrounded. A backgrounded simple command forks once and execs. `nohup` and the bin's `env node` shebang both exec in place, so `$!` is the server's `node` process.

Everything else is unchanged:
- the env (`OS_CLOUD_URL=off`), the arguments and the log redirection;
- the readiness loop, which still runs `kill -0` on the recorded PID at each poll;
- the `ready` line and the exit codes;
- `stop-backend.sh`, which still kills only the recorded PID. Nothing kills by port or by process name.

A comment above the hunk says why the `cd` must stay out of the backgrounded list.

## Reproduction (before: the base script at `96fa4b9bc`)

Setup for every run in this PR:
- this container: bash 5.2.21, Node 22.22.0, npm 10.9.4;
- `@objectstack/cli@18.0.0-next.2`;
- a fresh `LIVE_BACKEND_DIR` in the session scratchpad;
- port 4776, with nothing else on 4776 or 4777.

The base-script runs used `git show 96fa4b9bc:e2e/live/ci/start-backend.sh` byte for byte (blob `547ec18ab`).

1. **Start** (cold install, 137 s, exit 0) printed `ready: seeded sign-in answered on :4776 (pid 1092)`. The process tree from the recorded PID:
   - 1092 (PPID 1): `bash …/start-backend.sh`. This is the subshell.
   - 1093 (PPID 1092): `node ./node_modules/.bin/objectstack dev --seed-admin --fresh -p 4776`.
   - 1243 (PPID 1093): `node …/objectstack serve --dev --port 4776`. It holds the port.
   - 1285 (`esbuild --service`) and 1309 (`node ./scripts/mcp-fixture.mjs`): children of 1243.
2. **Stop**: `stop-backend.sh` printed `stopped pid 1092` and exited 0. `GET :4776/api/v1/health` still answered 200. 1092 was gone. 1093, 1243, 1285 and 1309 were all alive, and 1093's PPID was now 1.
3. **Start twice, no stop**:
   - The first run recorded 1433, a subshell over the server 1434.
   - The second run printed `starting objectstack dev on :4776`, not `already running`. The guard greps the recorded PID's cmdline for `objectstack`, and the subshell's cmdline is the script's own.
   - The second run recorded 1552, a subshell over a second server, 1553. That server logged `Port 4776 is in use — serving on 4777 instead.` and bound 4777.
   - The second run still printed `ready … on :4776 (pid 1552)` after 3 s. The FIRST server answered that check.

Each leftover server was then stopped by the PID read above: `kill 1093`, then `kill 1434 1553`. Each tree was gone within seconds, and both ports then refused connections.

## Proof (after: this branch at `3a0843dcf`)

The same `LIVE_BACKEND_DIR` (its stamp was reused) and the same port.

1. **Start** (19 s, exit 0) printed `ready: seeded sign-in answered on :4776 (pid 2201)`. `/proc/2201/cmdline` is `node ./node_modules/.bin/objectstack dev --seed-admin --fresh -p 4776`. The tree: 2201 (PPID 1), then 2221 (`objectstack serve --dev --port 4776`, the listener), then 2241 (`esbuild`) and 2252 (`mcp-fixture.mjs`).
2. **Start again** (1 s, exit 0) printed `[live-backend] already running (pid 2201)`. The PID file still read 2201, and only 2221 listened on 4776.
3. **Stop**: before it, `GET :4776/api/v1/health` answered 200. `stop-backend.sh` printed `stopped pid 2201` and exited 0. Straight after, health got curl exit 7 (connection refused), and the same 3 s later. 2201, 2221, 2241 and 2252 were all gone. No process listened on any 4xxx port. The SIGTERM to the `dev` process takes its `serve` child and the grandchildren down with it, so the recorded PID is enough.
4. **A boot that dies** (`LIVE_BACKEND_PORT=70000`): the CLI refused with `Invalid port: --port "70000"` and exited. The script printed `backend process died — last 100 log lines:` and exited 1 after 7 s. The base script on the same input gave the same line, exit 1, in 7 s. The readiness loop checks the recorded PID with `kill -0`. Before, that PID was a subshell, which lived exactly as long as its one child, the server. Now it is the server. So the fail-fast path answers the same on both sides.

## CI is unchanged

- `.github/workflows/live-e2e.yml` calls only `start-backend.sh`. `stop-backend.sh` appears there only in the comment `Ephemeral runner — no teardown needed`.
- `start-backend.sh` exits the same way and prints the same `ready` line on both sides: exit 0, and `[live-backend] ready: seeded sign-in answered on :PORT (pid N)`. Only N changes, from the subshell's PID to the server's.
- One visible difference, which does not change any verdict. The job's post-run orphan cleanup used to list a `bash` wrapper and then `node` (read on the objectui#12649 run). It should now list only the `node` processes. This was not measured on a runner. This PR's own `Live E2E (informational)` run will show it.

## Gates (local, at `3a0843dcf`, each exit captured before any pipe)

- `bash -n e2e/live/ci/start-backend.sh`: exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-bash32-floor.mjs`: exit 0, `13 tracked shell file(s) … name no bash 4+ construct`.
- `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs`: exit 0. A `grep -naP` self-scan of the changed file found no control byte.
- `node scripts/check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs`: exit 0, `0 new citation(s)`.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test e2e/live/ci/start-backend.sh`: exit 0, `NOT GOVERNED`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0, `no changeset is owed`. No `.changeset` file was added.
- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/bash32-floor-wiring.test.ts scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts`: `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 97 passed (97)`, lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`. These are the only test files that name `start-backend.sh` or `e2e/live/ci` (`git grep -l`).
- The doc-link check was not run, because no doc changed. `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` does not describe stopping the backend.

## Acceptance notes

- **No permanent test.** The behaviour needs a real backend. The before and after runs above are the proof: a one-off reading at `18.0.0-next.2`, which nothing in the tree re-derives (the comment says so too). No ablation, because no test pins this behaviour.
- **Boundary, not measured.** `stop-backend.sh` falls back to `kill -9` after 10 s, and that hits only the recorded `dev` process. If `dev` ever ignored SIGTERM, its `serve` child would be orphaned. This was not observed: in every run here, SIGTERM ended the whole tree.
- **Observation, not filed (governed file, not touched).** `AGENTS.md`'s per-agent test-stack section tells you to stop only by your own recorded PID, but the command it gives in the same parenthesis is `kill $(lsof -ti tcp:PORT)`, which kills by port. Its service-discipline section says never to kill by port. Carrier: none.
- **Observation, not filed.** In this container, PID 1 reaps orphans late, and a zombie still answers `kill -0`. Liveness above was read from `ps` state, not from `kill -0`.
